questions.question: An earthworm of length 18 cm is crawling along a certain path with a speed of 4 cm/s. An insect overtakes the earthworm in 6 s. How fast (in cm/s) is the insect walking? Assume that they both are walking along parallel paths.
questions.solution:
Given: 

Length of the earthworm = 18 cm

Speed of the earthworm = 4 cm/s

An insect overtakes the earthworm in 6s

Concept used:

Time × Speed = Distance

Among two objects running in the same direction, if one crosses the other, the faster one basically crosses the length of the slower one and the relative speed in this particular case is the difference between the individual speed of the two objects. 

Calculation:

Let the speed of the insect be Q cm/s.

According to the question,

6 × (Q - 4) = 18

⇒ Q = 7

**∴ The speed of the insect is 7cm/s.**

Concept used:

Total = Average × Number of entities

questions.question: A solid right circular cone is cut into two parts by a plane parallel to its base and at a point one-third vertically below its vertex. What is the ratio of the volume of the smaller cone to that of the whole cone?
questions.solution:
Given:

A solid right circular cone is cut into two parts by a plane parallel to its base and at a point one-third vertically below its vertex.

Concept used:

The volume of a cone = (πR²H ÷ 3) 

R and H are the radius of the base and height of the cone respectively.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6eb349e472bf015bb11f893641549e0d5aace885cd913a405e4f0c4d53f13fa1.png] 

Let the radius of the base and the height of the solid circular cone be R and H units respectively.

Hence,

The height of the cone that is cut from the original cone = {H over 3} units

The radius of the cone that is cut from the original cone = {R over 3} units

Thus, the required ratio

{π ({R over 3})² {H over 3} over 3} : {π R² H over 3}

⇒ {1 over 81} : {1 over 3} 

⇒ 1 : 27

⇒ {1 over 27}

**∴ {1 over 27} is the ratio of the volume of the smaller cone to that of the whole cone.**

questions.question: To do a certain work, the ratio of the efficiencies of A and B is 5 ∶ 11. Working together, they can do the same work in 27(1)/(2) days. A and B work together for 20 days. C alone completes the remaining work in 18 days. C alone can do 75% of the original work in:
questions.solution:
Given:

The ratio of the efficiencies of A and B is 5 ∶ 11

Working together, they can do the same work in 27(1)/(2) days i.e. {55 over 2} days

A and B work together for 20 days

C alone completes the remaining work in 18 days

Concept used:

Total work = Work done each day × Total time taken (in days)

Calculation:

Let the common ratio of their efficiencies be Q.

So, A and B do each day 5Q & 11Q units respectively.

Thus, total work = {55 over 2} × (5Q + 11Q) = 440Q units

Now, work done in 20 days by A and B together = (5Q + 11Q) × 20 = 320Q units

Remaining work = 440Q - 320Q = 120Q

Hence, efficiency of C = 120Q ÷ 18 = {20Q over 3} units

Thus, C alone can do 75% of the original work in = (440Q × 75%) ÷ {20Q over 3} = 49(1)/(2) days

**∴ C alone can do 75% of the original work in 49(1)/(2) days.**

questions.question: A manufacturer marks the price of an article at Rs. 1,200. He sells it to a trader at a discount of 10%. The trader gets a further discount of 5% on his net payment for paying in cash. What amount (in Rs.) does the trader pay to the manufacturer?
questions.solution:
Given:

Marked price = Rs. 1200

Discounts given = 10% and 5%

Concept used:

If A% and B% discounts are given successively,

final discount = (A + B - {A × B} over 100)%

Selling Price = Marked Price - Discount

Calculation:

Final resultant discount for the trader = 10 + 5 - {10 × 5} over 100 = 14.5%

Hence, the amount paid by the trader to the manufacturer = 1200 - 1200 × 14.5% = Rs. 1026

**∴ The trader pay Rs. 1026 to the manufacturer.**

Area increased by 50%

Calculation:

Let the final height H₁ respectively.

Final Area = Initial Area × 1.5

⇒ H₁ = H × 1.1538 (approx)

Hence, the increment of height = {{(H × 1.1538) - H} over H} times 100\% ≈ 15.38%

**∴ The height must be increased by 15.38%.**

questions.question: John sold a watch to Sue at a gain of 20%, and Sue sold it to Rima at a profit of 10%. If Rima paid Rs. 2,178 for it, how much did John pay (in Rs.) for the watch?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the multiplying factor method for successive profits:

20% profit = +1/5 ⇒ Multiplier = 6/5

10% profit = +1/10 ⇒ Multiplier = 11/10

Initial Price × (6/5) × (11/10) = Final Price

CP × 66/50 = 2178 ⇒ CP = 2178 × 50/66 = 1650

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1650.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Profit% earned by John = 20%

Profit% earned by Sue = 10%

Amount paid by Rima = ₹2178

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d6c499fca68e0d9e493e3f1d8ce0f5d7cb4fa30acc66542747b626a36dcc343.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the cost price for John be x.

⇒ Selling price of John = Cost price of Sue = x × (100 + 20)/100 = 1.2x

⇒ Selling price of Sue = Cost price of Rima = 1.2x × (100 + 10)/100 = 1.32x

⇒ As Rima paid ₹2178, we can equate the values:

⇒ 1.32x = 2178

⇒ x = 2178 ÷ 1.32 = 217800 ÷ 132

⇒ x = 1650

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1650.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Profit/Loss Formula

If an article is sold successively at profits of p₁% and p₂%, the final price is calculated as CP × (1 + p₁/100) × (1 + p₂/100).

Net Effective Profit%

When two successive profits p₁% and p₂% are applied, the effective net profit is given by (p₁ + p₂ + p₁p₂/100)%. Here, 20 + 10 + (200/100) = 32% overall profit.

Multiplier Method

Multiplying factors streamline successive changes. A 20% gain gives a multiplier of 1.2, and a 10% gain gives 1.1. Combined multiplier = 1.2 × 1.1 = 1.32.

questions.question:
The sum of the height and radius of the base of a solid right circular cylinder is 46 cm. If the total surface area of the solid cylinder is 6072 cm², what is the volume (in cm³) of the cylinder?

(Use π = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
Given: 

The sum of the height and radius of the base of a solid right circular cylinder is 46 cm

The total surface area of the solid cylinder is 6072 cm

Concept used:

The surface area of a cylinder = 2πR (R + H)

The volume of a cylinder = πR²H 

Where R = Radius of the base, H = Height 

Calculation:

Let the height and radius of the base be H and R respectively.

Thus, R + H = 46

According to the question,

2πR × (R + H) = 6072

⇒ 2πR × 46 = 6072

⇒ R = 21

Hence, H = 46 - 21 = 25 cm

Thus, the volume of the cylinder = π × (21)² × 25 = 11025π cm²

**∴ The volume of the cylinder is 11025π cm²**.

The combined sales of the five companies in 2007-2008 = 1650 + 1350 + 1000 + 1760 + 1440 = 7200 Cr.

Hence, % difference = {(7200 - 6080) over 7200} times 100\% approx 15.56\%

**∴ 15.56% is the percentage difference of the combined sales of the five companies in 2008-2009 compared to the combined sales of the five companies in 2007-2008.**

questions.question: On selling a bat for Rs. 954, a man gains 6%. What should be its selling price (in Rs.) to gain 8%?
questions.solution:
Given:

By selling at Rs. 954, the gain is 6%.

Desired gain is 8%.

Concept used:

Selling Price = Cost Price (1 + Profit%)

Calculation:

Cost Price of the bat = 954 ÷ (1 + 0.06) = Rs. 900

Hence, to make 8% gain, the selling price must be = 900 × (1 + 0.08) = Rs. 972

**∴ Its selling price to gain 8% should be Rs. 972.**
